title: Violet Fault Spire
description: A seven-metre violet blade growing with smaller intergrown crystals from a displaced limestone fissure; references: ref_07_violet_crater and ref_03_canyon_cliffs.

review.notes: Round 1: rejected. Failing: (1) silhouette/style: the spire is one smooth, straight, symmetrical prism with a pointed cap, so it reads as a purple obelisk or plastic monument rather than a crystal; the three side crystals are too small to balance it (sheet turns, hero). (2) form_detail 6: the main body has almost no readable facets or growth lines, only a smooth dark-to-light gradient; no steps, terminations or fractures (closeup_upper). (3) material 7: no dark core, inner bands or bright veins. (4) defects 7: the base is a ring of clean white boxy blocks with flat cut faces, like sugar cubes, set loosely around a dark soil patch; they do not read as the fault rock the spire grows out of (closeup_base). Fix: lean and taper the spire, break it into a main prism with 2-3 intergrown secondary prisms and one broken termination; carve stepped growth faces; give it the dark core, inner bands and veins; replace the block ring with a split, weathered limestone outcrop the crystal emerges from, with soil and grass in the cracks.
